rulings: Task 1: Ruling: include the identical shadow packing defect in this fix — the required full lighting probe now reaches and fails its existing overflow parity check; same private 128-bit layout remedy preserves the shadow contract — cost if wrong: regression in cascade/temporal rendering, covered by exact layer, draw and lifecycle tests on both backends.

Task 1: Ruling: keep SwiftShader terminator lighting as the next separate audit defect, not a packing regression — full lighting now reaches `terminator finite marched HDR`; isolated original/candidate runs have byte-identical fixture source and identical sampled outputs (NaN RGB/shadow, alpha 1.001953125, finite depth 43104/43264), both release all textures — cost if wrong: software lighting remains broken despite a complete packing fix; full SwiftShader lighting is explicitly not claimed green.

Task 1: Ruling: rerun timing-sensitive pipeline probes sequentially — native lighting passed 2083 checks, but simultaneous SwiftShader diagnosis coincided with a 250.5ms preparation slice failure; no timeout or timing thresholds changed — cost if wrong: a real scheduling regression could recur; retain the failed report and require the unchanged timing gate to pass.

Task 1: Ruling: validate the completed SwiftShader pipeline from its retained raw report without repeating rendering — exact four rendering/warning ReadPixels notices caused the collector failure; independent validation accepts that precise message class and requires all functional cases, resources, no runtime/network errors, exact known shader identities and timestamp-bounded intentional invalid-program logs — cost if wrong: misclassified diagnostics could hide a failure; negative controls reject unknown shader/console logs and invalid programs outside their windows, and the original exit 1 remains archived.

Final: Ruling: retain terminator repair as the next audit item — reviewer confirms original/candidate equality supports a pre-existing defect, without establishing its cause — cost if wrong: software terminator HDR/shadows remain unusable; full lighting stays explicitly failed.

Final: Ruling: preserve ordinary MRT overflow semantics — sanitizing nonfinite depth changes the reference output contract and is not required to remove packing contamination — cost if wrong: out-of-range depth can still be nonfinite on a backend.

Final: Ruling: leave the 250.5ms spike cause unresolved — an unchanged sequential gate passed but does not prove contention caused the failure — cost if wrong: rare preparation stalls may recur and need separate diagnosis.

Final: Ruling: retain reviewed inherited warnings — exact sources/logs and the define-only Bayer variant establish provenance, not universal numerical correctness — cost if wrong: an underlying shader issue could remain; unknown diagnostics still fail validation.
